requirements.title: Declare the concentration
requirements.summary: Choose a concentration as early as possible, and no later than the second semester of sophomore year before third-year registration. No advisor approval is required to select one; changing it later may delay graduation. The default traditional BS and its advisor-approved focus area are separate paths.

requirements.title: Independent-study exclusion
requirements.summary: Independent study cannot be used as a concentration course. Its separate use as a CISC elective or in an advisor-approved traditional focus area does not establish AI/Robotics concentration credit.

requirements.title: Pass/fail and audit restrictions
requirements.summary: Pass/fail coursework cannot meet major or minor requirements. Audited courses earn no credit. No concentration-specific minimum grade is established by this FAQ.

requirements.title: Exceptions and substitutions
requirements.summary: Department permission is required for exceptional substitutions. A different course requires the Course Requirement Substitution Form; other exceptions go to the Undergraduate Curriculum and Program Committee.

requirements.title: Applicable catalog edition
requirements.summary: The university catalog controls degree requirements; use the student’s matriculation-year program description unless the student has changed to a later catalog year. Detailed current AI/Robotics course choices remain unverified.

notes: The public BS page confirms a transcript-recognized AI and Robotics concentration. The current course core, finite elective pool, selection counts and grade/overlap constraints remain unverified because detailed standard/honors links point to the known restricted catalog. The catalog was not retried.

An independently public departmental committee FAQ provides declaration timing, lack of advisor approval for choosing a formal concentration, the independent-study exclusion, pass/fail/audit limits, exception handling and applicable catalog-year rules. The FAQ is undated and includes historical program examples; these observations do not replace the controlling catalog.

The committee technical-elective page records CISC440 Computer Graphics under Spring 2025, CISC367-012 Introduction to Mobile Robot Programming under Fall 2024, and CISC367-012 Introduction to Robot Programming under Summer 2024 as AI/Robotics restricted electives. These dated approvals are not treated as the current complete pool or promoted to required-course records.

The traditional BS focus area is informal, separately advisor-approved and permits some independent-study credit; those rules do not apply to the formal AI/Robotics concentration. Standard and honors catalog links do not alone establish separate AI program identities. First-offered date remains unknown.
